sources.entry: Nextcloud | Productivity platform for file hosting and collaboration

summary.one_liner: Official-style Docker image packaging the Nextcloud file hosting and collaboration server in Apache and PHP-FPM variants, maintained by community volunteers.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts for the Nextcloud image, offered as an apache tag (full Nextcloud with a built-in web server on port 80) and an fpm tag (PHP-FPM on port 9000 that needs a separate web server such as nginx to proxy to it). The README documents configuration through environment variables covering database setup (SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL), an initial admin account, Redis caching, SMTP mail, and S3 or OpenStack Swift object storage as primary storage. It also covers PHP and Apache limits, reverse-proxy and trusted-proxy settings, Docker secrets via _FILE variables, and hook folders for pre/post install, upgrade and start scripts. Docker compose examples, volume layouts for data/config/custom_apps, occ command usage, and upgrade and migration steps are included. The README notes that the image is community-maintained and points users to the Nextcloud All-in-One container for a full-featured deployment.
use_cases: self-host a personal cloud file sync server
share files and calendars with a team using Docker
run Nextcloud behind an nginx or reverse proxy
configure Nextcloud with a MariaDB or PostgreSQL database in compose
store Nextcloud user data in S3 or Swift object storage
automate Nextcloud installation with environment variables
migrate an existing Nextcloud install into Docker
how_to_run: docker compose up -d  (using a compose.yaml with the apache or fpm example)
docker compose exec -u33 app ./occ config:list system
docker compose pull && docker compose up -d  (to update)
notable: Two image variants: apache (all-in-one web server) and fpm (for pairing with a separate web server)
Full auto-configuration via environment variables, bypassing the web setup wizard
Hook folders (pre-installation, post-upgrade, before-starting, etc.) for custom scripts
Object storage support for S3-compatible and OpenStack Swift as primary storage
Docker secrets support via _FILE environment variables
caveats: The README states the image is maintained by community volunteers and designed for expert use; the Nextcloud All-in-One container is recommended for quick deployment with the full Hub feature set
Upgrades must be done one major version at a time
Data in /var/www/html is overwritten during upgrades unless listed in upgrade.exclude; custom volumes need care
